newsitem.title: USA: LL&E plans additional Algeria wells.
newsitem.headline: LL&E plans additional Algeria wells.

text.p: Louisiana Land & Exploration Co plans to drill several additional wells in its Algeria oil play next year after dissapointing results this year, John Williams, senior vice president of exploration and production, said on Tuesday.
"We're dealing with a more complex resevoir than we all thought we were dealing with," Williams said in a presentation at the Rauscher Pierce Refsnes Inc energy conference in Houston.

The MLN-1 well at three intervals tested at 15,850 barrels of oil per day and 61 million cubic feet per day of natural gas in 85 feet of net pay, he said. But exploratory drilling in the prospect also discovered poorly developed sands in the oil column and an uncertain water level in the field.
The New Orleans, Louisiana-based independent oil and gas company expects to drill three or four additional wells there next year, depending on the success of the MLN-2 well, he said.

In the United States, LL&E sees the possibility of boosting proven reserves in its Wyoming natural gas play to 800 to 900 billion cubic feet from the current 200 billion cubic feet from exploratory drilling in the Madden Field.
The additional reserves should be coming on line at the same time two separate pipeline expansion projects boost delivery out of the Rockies by more than 300 million cubic feet per day, he said.
"Hopefully, we'll have this timed rather well for pulling both sweet gas and sour gas out of the Madden area," he said.
LL&E boosted its exploration and development budget this year to $240 million from $210 million, largely to step up three-dimensional seismic acquisitions and exploration in the U.S. Gulf.
The company will be actively bidding in the upcoming U.S. Gulf deepwater lease round in the western section of the gulf, Williams said.
